paper_metadata.title: High-Temperature Three-Point Bending Property of Ti60 Alloy Rolled Sheet Before and After Vacuum Solution Aging Treatment

evidence.quote: As a new near-α-type alloy developed for the aerospace field, Ti60 alloy is expected to be widely used in the future

other.interpass: replaced into furnace for heat retention after each pass

evidence.quote: The material underwent rolling at 1000 °C via the multidirectional rolling approach for eight passes. After each pass, it was replaced into the furnace for heat retention.
Eventually, annealing at 600 °C for 4 h yielded the as-rolled Ti60 alloy.

Solution treatment was carried out at 1090 °C for 2 h, followed by aging treatment at 700 °C for 2 h. Their heating rate is 10 °C min/C0 1. Both treatments were air-cooled to room temperature (20 °C) at cooling rates of 4.3 and 2.7 °C s /C0 1, respectively.

the microstructure of the original rolled sheet is mainly composed of primary α phase and flocculent α phase.
It can be seen from Figure 7a,b that the original rolled sheet is equiaxed fine grain structure.
the average grain area in Figure 7a is 16.69 μm2.
The original rolled sheet has a strong {0001}<10-10> texture with a texture strength of 9.08
treated by 1090 °C/2 h/AC þ 700 °C/2 h/AC vacuum solution aging treatment, the microstructure becomes Widmanstatten microstructure dominated by lamellar structure.
The average grain area in Figure 7b is 80.98 μm2.
the α-Ti phase pole figure of the vacuum solution aging-treated rolled sheet after the three-point bending test shows that it has a strong {11-20}<0001> texture.
the texture intensity increased from 9.08 to 45.59.
The lamellar structure of Ti60 alloy is composed of lamellar colony with different orientations, and there is an interface between the lamellar colony.
the Widmanstatten microstructure contains a large number of Σ11 twin grain boundary.
the grains on both sides of the Σ11 twin grain boundary rotate around the <11-20> axis by 50.48°
There are many holes near the tip of the crack in Figure 5d; it shows that the tip of the crack propagation belongs to the microvoid aggregation fracture.
It can be seen from Figure 6f that a hole is generated before the crack propagation, and the crack propagation path passes through the hole.

When the crack propagation encounters the lamellar interface, the crack propagation direction will be hindered and changed due to the different crystal orientations of different lamellae. In order to continue to expand, the crack needs to consume additional energy to bypass or pass through the lamellae, which makes the crack propagation path become tortuous.
